issues: "Trump, Musk and Zelenskyy trade blame over Ukraine's Starlink access" is a cosmetic edit of the original's "who is blaming who ... erupted" — same subject and angle (the blame dispute), words swapped, no genuine reframing.

"Residents told to shut windows as officials respond to River Taff kerosene leak" still centres the headline on the leak itself in an "as ... respond" clause — the pattern the brief explicitly fails (cf. "Rail unions call for more staff ... as reported assaults hit record high"); the only response shown is a precautionary advisory to shut windows, a weak response that per the brief should not put the leak in the headline at all, or should be scored as a 0/1 story instead.

"new effects" is vague and drops the original's specific claims — the original names "Raging Bull" and "a Toy Story vibe" as the specific other influences on the refresh, which the rewrite replaces with a generic phrase.

"Approving the Jackdaw gasfield is part of making net zero work for Britain" merely reorders the clauses of the original's "We will make the net-zero transition work for Britain – approving the Jackdaw gasfield is part of the plan" — same subject and angle, a cosmetic edit.
"the movement could outflank" drops the original's "could fatally outflank the prime minister" — removing "fatally" understates how severe the threat to Meloni is described as being.
"Tech firms that profit from the internet" drops the original's specific claim that these firms "make billions from it", weakening a scale claim into vagueness.

The setback named in the original headline, "The internet has broken – again", is dropped entirely rather than moved to the standfirst — the rewrite's headline and trail mention only the vaguer "vulnerabilities", so a reader of the headline-and-trail pair is never told the bad news plainly.

"searching for purpose but not yet self-awareness" adds "yet", implying a future self-awareness the original does not suggest — the original flatly says "not self-awareness" with no hint of eventual change.
"other readers add their own experiences" drops the original's named letter-writers "Mark Hanson, Paul Whiteing", replacing them with an unnamed generic group.

"as a model Britain could follow" is an inference added beyond the original, which only says Melding "highlights how New Zealand has created" its healthcare culture, without saying Britain should follow it.

"entrenches sectarian politics" attributes a specific causal claim to Boyd Black that the original does not state — the original only says he "deplores" Labour's policy, not that he argues it entrenches sectarian politics.
